title: feat(core): curate `object-tree` onto the public tier, where the spec already declares it (objectui#10064)
body:
Fixes #10064

Executes ruling batch #197 item 1 letter A. `object-tree` joins the curated public tier.

## What was wrong, stated as the direction it was wrong in

`@objectstack/spec` **declares** `object-tree` on `ComponentPropsMap`, and `@object-ui/plugin-tree` has registered the renderer all along. The curated `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` roster — `packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts` — carried no tree name, so `getPublicConfigs()` reported the block as outside the contract. The public tier sat **narrower than the declaration**.

Everything downstream reported that faithfully and none of it could repair it: `getPublicConfigs()` is the read both manifest producers serialize through `manifestFromConfigs`, so the framework's tracked manifest could never carry a block the contract says exists, and moving the objectui pin could not help while the pinned source had nothing to carry.

⇒ this is a **narrowing being undone, not a widening**: the accepted set does not grow past the declaration, it stops being smaller than it. `Clause-②: no`, on that reasoning.

## What decides membership of the public tier — measured before changing anything

`Registry.getPublicConfigs()` admits a block by exactly **two** routes:

1. membership of the curated `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` roster, resolved through `getContractConfig(tag)` (a listed tag with no registration behind it is skipped silently);
2. `tier: 'public'` declared on the registration itself, for bare (non-namespaced) keys, including pending lazy stubs.

**The siblings settle which one this is.** Every curated view block — `object-grid`, `object-map`, `object-gantt`, … — reaches the tier through the roster, and **no registration in this repo's published source declares `tier: 'public'`**; the only hits for that flag are four test fixtures. The roster's own header asks callers to prefer the list over scattered flags. So the admission is a roster entry, ⛔ not a flag, and ⛔ not both.

**PM mechanism assumption B, tested: there is no recorded exclusion.** `public-blocks.ts` records six deliberate exclusions by name (`record:chatter`, `action:bar`, `element:image`, `element:record_picker`, `element:text_input`, `element:metadata_viewer`) and the console's reverse-coverage guard carries the same six with reasons. No tree name appears in either, and the reverse-coverage sweep is scoped to the four semantic namespaces (`record` / `page` / `element` / `action`), so a `plugin-tree`-namespaced block was never in a population any forcing function looked at. This is an omission, not a decision — so it is a fix, not a decision card.

## Reproduced with a lit control before repairing

The card's readings were relayed from the objectstack#18407 dev at a pinned objectui sha and were ⛔ not re-run by the filing seat. Re-taken here on this branch's base, `516583b54`, by `packages/plugin-tree/src/registration.publicTier-10064.test.tsx` before the roster was touched:

```
FAIL  object-tree on the curated public tier > curates object-tree beside its sibling view blocks
AssertionError: expected [ 'object-grid', 'list-view', …(56) ] to include 'object-tree'
FAIL  … > reports object-tree through the read both manifest producers serialize
AssertionError: expected [ 'record:details', …(41) ] to include 'object-tree'
FAIL  … > carries the block real inputs, not a propless entry
AssertionError: expected [] to include 'objectName'
Tests  3 failed | 2 passed (5)
```

The lit control passes on the line above each failure: `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` answers `object-grid`, so a zero for the tree is an absence the instrument could see, ⛔ not a failed lookup. One number differs from the relayed reading and the direction does not: the roster holds **58** entries on today's `main`, not the 57 recorded at the pinned sha — zero tree names either way.

## The repair

One roster entry, beside the view-plugin family it belongs to, carrying the reasoning above.

The bare `tree` alias the same module registers **stays out, deliberately and not by omission** — triage asked for that answer explicitly. The spec declares no such key, so curating it would widen the vocabulary **past** the declaration (the opposite act, and a clause-② `yes`), and two spellings of one block is ambiguity an authoring model cannot resolve — the ground `record:chatter` is held out on. The pin asserts the alias is registered, is absent from the roster, and is absent from `getPublicConfigs()`, so withholding it is now a reviewable decision rather than a silence.

## Ablation — the admission removed, on disk, with both legs proven

Run from the committed fix. The mutation deletes the one roster line; the anchor count is asserted **1** before and **0** after, and the on-disk blob hash moves:

```
HEAD blob: 73659fca18f2742dcb195dfa806b91d14e43e568
admission lines before mutation: 1
admission lines after mutation: 0
mutated blob: da6c6862fd71262cda146b59ab385fa6a4553fb8
control — the roster is otherwise intact: object-grid still 1
```

**The manifest loses the block.** A one-shot probe (deleted after the reading, ⛔ not committed) mirrors what both producers do — eager-register the 16 registry modules in `manifest-dump`'s order, read `getPublicConfigs()`, refuse pending stubs with `assertFullyLoaded`, serialize through `manifestFromConfigs`:

```
fixed    : ABLATION-PROBE blocks=59 object-grid=true object-tree=true tree=false
ablated  : ABLATION-PROBE blocks=58 object-grid=true object-tree=false tree=false
```

**The pin reds**, 3 failed / 2 passed, with the control assertions still green.

**The restore is proven, not assumed.** `git checkout HEAD -- packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts`, then: `git diff HEAD` empty, on-disk hash back to `73659fca18f2742dcb195dfa806b91d14e43e568`, admission line count back to 1, and the pin green again at 5 passed.

## Consequences, reported rather than absorbed

The card asked for any render, bundle-size or docs consequence of the block becoming public. Three measured, one noted.

- **Render / binding — measured, and it passes.** Admitting the block pulls it into the derived population of `public-block-binding-reach`, which mounts each curated block declaring an `objectName` under a recording data source: `object-tree asks the data layer for its objectName` — a real fetch, no error card. It also joins the `kind:'react'` page scope as the derived identifier `ObjectTree` (that scope is built from the same public configs minus declared containers; this block declares no containment).
- **Bundle — measured over a real console build, and nothing moves.** The console registers the block **lazily** and `getPublicConfigs()` resolves the stub without loading the chunk, so the plugin stays out of the initial bundle: `check:eager-closure` reports 3033.2 KB gzipped across 329 of 2310 chunks against a 3104.5 KB budget, and the string `plugin-tree` appears **0 times** in that report while the control `ui-components` appears 3 — the instrument does name eager chunks, and this is not one. The console pin records the same fact from the other side: the block arrives `lazy: true` with `component: undefined`.
- **Docs — one consequence, ⛔ not repaired here, see Acceptance notes.**
- **Contract-side — nothing to widen.** `registry-inputs-spec-parity` is SPEC-shaped (`Object.keys(ComponentPropsMap)` filtered to what this repo registers with inputs) and never reads the roster, so this admission opens no new population there; the spec already carries the key.

## Scope — one declared extension, named rather than absorbed

The claim's file surface is `packages/plugin-tree/` and the public-block registry. Two files outside it are in this diff, and both are **mechanically forced** by the roster edit rather than chosen: `apps/console/src/__tests__/public-contract.test.ts` and `apps/console/src/__tests__/public-block-binding-reach.test.tsx` assert **exact lists** over the same roster (deliberately, because the failure mode they guard is a *shrinking* contract), so the change cannot be green without them. Both edits are the one-line list entry the failing assertion prints, plus the reason. Held by no other claim in this lane. Reported in the dev report as a deviation.

## Acceptance notes

- **noted, not filed — `content/docs/guide/react-pages.md` uses this block as its specimen for the escape hatch.** The `Block` section is headed "Any registered component, including ones outside the public contract" and its example is `Block type="object-tree"`. The sentence stays literally true and `Block` still renders any registered type, but the specimen is now *inside* the contract, so the example no longer illustrates the case it was chosen for. ⛔ Not repaired here: the page is outside this card's surface and nothing it asserts becomes false. Carrier: the next change to that guide page, or the docs half of the objectstack#18407 chain. Class (c) is ⛔ not claimed — no authoring metadata is refused or dropped.
- **noted, not filed — the reverse-coverage forcing function cannot see this class.** `public-contract.test.ts` sweeps only the `record` / `page` / `element` / `action` namespaces for "shipped but uncurated", so a block registered under a plugin namespace can never fail it by absence — which is how this one sat uncurated with no ledger entry and no red. Widening that sweep is a decision about what the ledger is for, not a repair; it also does not follow from this card. Carrier: whoever next edits that guard's `SEMANTIC_NAMESPACES`.
- Base of this branch is `516583b54`; the eslint reading below is from the final commit.

## Verification

Vitest is run from the repo root, exit codes captured to a file and read back.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/ packages/plugin-tree/` | 177 files, 3466 tests passed — exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/ …react-page-scope, container-declaration-census, container-declaration-ratchet` | 32 files, 500 tests passed — exit 0 |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/core --filter=@object-ui/plugin-tree` | 15 tasks successful — exit 0 |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/console` | 36 tasks successful — exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` | 8708 modules transformed — exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:sdui-registration-pins` | all 16 promised registrations present over that build, 2310 chunks weighed — exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:eager-closure` | 3033.2 KB / 3104.5 KB budget — exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:side-effects-array` · `check:dist-completeness` | exit 0; dist-completeness now weighs 12 built packages, 1661 emitted files |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 8190 tracked text files scanned — exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:component-surface-parity` · `check:changeset-claims` · `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 (all three report-only by their own headers) |
| `pnpm check:registry-bare-names` · `check:doc-types` · `check:prompt-keys` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` · `pnpm changeset:check` | exit 0; one changeset declared, no `major` |

**Lint is a declared narrowing, and here is why it is a measurement.** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the four changed source files: **4 files linted**, 0 errors, 5 warnings — all five are pre-existing `no-explicit-any` hits in `public-block-binding-reach.test.tsx`, none on a line this branch adds. The population is read from eslint's own config resolution, not guessed: none of the three packages carries its own `eslint.config.*`, so each one's `eslint .` resolves the same root flat config this invocation used. **Type-aware linting is not enabled** — the root config extends `tseslint.configs.recommended` with no `project` / `projectService` / `…TypeChecked` anywhere — so no verdict on an untouched file can move because of this diff, which is what makes the narrowing safe rather than merely smaller. The repo-wide sweep is CI's run.

Heavy runs were serialized through the shared verify lock; `check:*` gates are not covered by it and ran alongside other work, so no timing here is an idle-box figure.
